body:
The current [Docker integration guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker) recommends installing dependencies into a virtual environment (`/app/.venv`) and copying it to the final stage:

```dockerfile
FROM python:alpine AS builder
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest /uv /uvx /bin/
ENV UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=0
WORKDIR /app
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    --mount=type=bind,source=uv.lock,target=uv.lock \
    uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --no-editable
COPY . /app
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --locked --no-editable

FROM python:alpine
COPY --from=builder /app/.venv /app/.venv
CMD ["/app/.venv/bin/myapp"]

```

### The Problem

My application has optional features that rely on extra packages installed by users at runtime:

```python
try:
    from PIL import Image
except ImportError:
    Image = None
else:
    # functionality requiring pillow

```

When users install packages in the container using standard commands (e.g., `pip install pillow`), those packages are installed into the global environment (e.g., `/usr/local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/`). Because `myapp` runs inside the isolated `/app/.venv` virtual environment, it cannot see or import any user-installed global packages.

Previously, when building Docker images without `uv`, we installed packages globally into the container's system Python, which avoided this issue completely.

### Suggestion

1. **At lease document this limitation:** The Docker guide should explicitly note that using an isolated `.venv` prevents the application from accessing packages installed into the global system environment later.
2. **Recommend system-level installation:** Since containers already provide isolation, it would be better to update the primary examples to install into the system Python environment, preventing users from running into this trap.
title: Recommended Docker `.venv` workflow isolates app from user-installed system packages at runtime
